author: GamingBolt
description:
While Saber Interactive is known for games where you control heavy machinery in challenging situations like RoadCraft and SnowRunner, with Docked, the studio has taken a different approach. 

Rather than being a jack-of-all-trades, your focus is instead narrower, running an efficient port and building up to eventually thrive. In gameplay terms, this also means that most of the gameplay revolves around the use of varying types of cranes. 

In practice, the crane gameplay feels quite engaging, and the sheer complexity of these machines tend to also provide a hefty sense of satisfaction from having mastered a certain task. This is paired with a light layer of management gameplay where you’re signing deals, upgrading buildings and buying more vehicles. 

However, despite the level of attention paid to cranes and other dock vehicles, there is also a general lack of variety that might end up doing more harm than good in the long term.
title: Docked Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
There’s a reason as to why the word Tyrant still carries weight for every Resident Evil fan. It’s been three decades since players first found themselves locked inside the claustrophobic corridors of the Spencer Mansion. You might have forgotten the zombies, or even the lethal hunters - but the Tyrant was just built differently. It wasn’t just another monster - it was the grand reveal; the moment you realized that the evil Umbrella Corp hadn’t lost control of its experiments but had achieved its goal.

Tyrants are not random mutations. They are the end product of the t-Virus program - human-based bio-organic weapons engineered for battlefield use. Tyrants are strong enough to tear through steel doors, intelligent enough to follow commands, and durable enough to absorb punishment that would level buildings. In gameplay terms, they mark a shift from survival horror chaos to something more focused and more terrifying - the feeling of being hunted by design.
title: Resident Evil’s Tyrants Explained - The Horrifying Origins of Umbrella’s Ultimate Weapons

author: GamingBolt
description:
Dissecting Resident Evil’s history is no easy task. Fifteen years ago, this might have been an autopsy – a post-mortem in the wake of Resident Evil 6 when the series seemed to lose direction. But, in the time since, through bold reinventions and a string of exceptional remakes like RE2 and RE1, the developer has clawed the series back to vitality. 

But now, the inevitable question: what actually makes a good Resident Evil game? Is it tense survival horror? Tactical action? Intricate resource management? Or a delicate balance between all three? Truth is, Resident Evil is thriving because it veers between each philosophy, sometimes within the same game.
title: We Ranked Every Mainline Resident Evil Game - From The Worst To The Best
